# Implementation of an AND Logic Gate Using Switches                                    on a Dot Board

&nbsp;

## Aim:

To construct, wire, and solder a switch-based two-input AND logic gate circuit on a general-purpose dot board (perfboard) and experimentally verify its operational truth table using an LED indicator.

&nbsp;

#### Principle & Working

The switch-based AND gate implements the Boolean logic function Y \= SW1\*SW2 through a series-connected electrical circuit. In digital logic representation, an open switch corresponds to Logic 0 (OFF), a closed switch denotes Logic 1 (ON), and the state of the output is indicated by the LED, where an unlit diode signifies Logic 0 and an illuminated diode signifies Logic 1\. Because electrical loads require a continuous, closed conductive loop between the positive and negative terminals of the power supply to function, the operation of this circuit depends entirely on the simultaneous closure of both series switches. When both switches remain open, or when either SW1 or SW2 is closed independently while the other is left open, the loop is broken by an air gap, creating an open circuit that blocks current flow (I \= 0\) and leaves the LED unlit. Only when both SW1 and SW2 are closed together does a complete conductive path form from the positive terminal of the 9V battery through the switches, the anode of the LED, and the current-limiting resistor back to the negative terminal. This complete loop forward-biases the LED, driving sufficient current to illuminate it while the series resistor limits the current to a safe operating level, thereby demonstrating that a high output occurs exclusively when all series inputs are simultaneously high.&nbsp;
